### Contemporary period (1949 - Present)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kottayam&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Contemporary period (1949 - Present)")]

Kottayam became a revenue division of Travancore.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kottayam#cite_note-Kurien-10) A fifth division, [Devikulam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Devikulam "Devikulam"), existed for a short period but was later added to Kottayam. Kottayam district established in July 1949.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kottayam#cite_note-15)

## Geography

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kottayam&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Geography")]

[![Image 14](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/3c/Purple_Swamphen_%28Porphyrio_poliocephalus%29_22-Mar-2007_10-12-15_AM.jpg/250px-Purple_Swamphen_%28Porphyrio_poliocephalus%29_22-Mar-2007_10-12-15_AM.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Purple_Swamphen_(Porphyrio_poliocephalus)_22-Mar-2007_10-12-15_AM.jpg)

Purple Swamphen (_[Porphyrio porphyrio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Porphyrio\_porphyrio "Porphyrio porphyrio")_) photographed in Vembanad Lake, Kottayam

Kottayam has an average elevation of 3 metres (9.8 ft) above sea level.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kottayam#cite_note-16) It is situated in the [basin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drainage_basin "Drainage basin") of the [Meenachil River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meenachil_River "Meenachil River") and in the basin of the [Vembanad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vembanad "Vembanad") backwaters, which are formed from several streams in the [Western Ghats](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Western_Ghats "Western Ghats") of the [Idukki district](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Idukki_district "Idukki district"). The town is situated near the inland [estuary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Estuary "Estuary") of [Meenachil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meenachil_River "Meenachil River") river where it empties into the [Vembanad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vembanad "Vembanad") lake in [Kumarakom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kumarakom "Kumarakom").

According to the division of places in Kerala based on altitudes, Kottayam is classified as a midland area. The general soil type is [alluvial](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alluvium "Alluvium") soil. The vegetation is mainly tropical evergreen and moist deciduous. The district features a mix of hills, back waters and paddy fields.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kottayam#cite_note-17)

The area under Kottayam Municipality is 55.40 square kilometers. Kottayam town, the headquarters of Kottayam district is situated in the central part of Kerala, in the Central Travancore region. It is situated in between 9°29' 46" N and 9º 37' 59" North latitude and 76°29' 22" E and 76°34' 24" East longitudes.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kottayam#cite_note-18)

### Climate

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kottayam&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Climate")]

Under the [Köppen climate classification](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/K%C3%B6ppen_climate_classification "Köppen climate classification"), Kottayam has a [Tropical monsoon climate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropical_monsoon_climate "Tropical monsoon climate") (Am).

The climate in this district is moderate and pleasant. Kottayam's proximity to the equator results in little seasonal temperature variation, with moderate to high levels of humidity year-round.

Kottayam district is bordered by [Pathanamthitta district](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pathanamthitta_district "Pathanamthitta district") on the south, [Alappuzha district](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alappuzha_district "Alappuzha district") on the west, [Ernakulam district](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ernakulam_district "Ernakulam district") on the north and [Idukki district](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Idukki_district "Idukki district") on the east and northeast.

**Agriculture**

Kottayam district is a significant center for natural rubber cultivation in Kerala. The headquarters of the **Rubber Board** (a statutory body under the Government of India) is located in Kottayam, which plays a key role in the development of the rubber industry.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kottayam#cite_note-22)

Rubber is the dominant cash crop, with the district contributing substantially to Kerala's production (Kerala accounts for the majority of India's natural rubber output).[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kottayam#cite_note-23) In addition to rubber, secondary crops include coconut, banana, pineapple, pepper, and various spices. Intercropping in rubber plantations with vegetables and other short-term crops is encouraged for additional income.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kottayam#cite_note-24)

## Literature

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kottayam&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Literature")]

_Jnananikshepam_ was the first newspaper published by the natives of Kerala, published at CMS press at Kottayam in 1848.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kottayam#cite_note-29) Kottayam has produced many well-known writers, journalists and artists. Novelist [Muttathu Varkey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Muttathu_Varkey "Muttathu Varkey") and poet [Pala Narayanan Nair](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pala_Narayanan_Nair "Pala Narayanan Nair") both have roots in Kottayam. [Kottayam Pushpanath](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kottayam_Pushpanath "Kottayam Pushpanath"), a writer of crime thrillers lived in Kottayam. He died due to age related ailments on 2 May 2018.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kottayam#cite_note-30) The Indian-English novelist [Arundhati Roy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arundhati_Roy "Arundhati Roy") is a native of Kottayam[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kottayam#cite_note-31) and her semi-autobiographical Booker Prize-winning novel, _[The God of Small Things](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_God\_of\_Small\_Things "The God of Small Things"),_ contains her childhood experiences in [Aymanam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aymanam "Aymanam"), Kottayam. [Unni R.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unni_R. "Unni R.") a story writer and scriptwriter, is also from Kottayam. Kottayam was the first town in India to have achieved 100% literacy.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kottayam#cite_note-32) Kottayam Public Library was founded in 1882 by T Rama RaoDewanPeshkar (Collector) of Northern Division of Travancore State.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kottayam#cite_note-33)

## Education

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kottayam&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Education")]

In the 17th century, a Dutch school was started at Kottayam, which was short-lived. The first English school in Kerala, and the first college in India, was established in 1817 by the [Church Missionary Society](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Church_Missionary_Society "Church Missionary Society") of England under the leadership of [Col. John Munro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Munro,_9th_of_Teaninich "John Munro, 9th of Teaninich"), as [CMS College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CMS_College_Kottayam "CMS College Kottayam").[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kottayam#cite_note-cms-14) Today CMS College Kottayam and [SB College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Berchmans_College "St. Berchmans College"), established with help of Syro Malabar Catholic Church, in [Changanassery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Changanassery "Changanassery"), 17 km from town, stands as a landmark and has made a huge contribution to education in the district. Thus, Kottayam became India's first town with 100% literacy in 1989.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kottayam#cite_note-34)

The [Government Medical College, Kottayam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Government_Medical_College,_Kottayam "Government Medical College, Kottayam"), is one of the most prominent medical colleges in Kerala. Also, [Mahatma Gandhi University, Kerala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mahatma_Gandhi_University,_Kerala "Mahatma Gandhi University, Kerala"), is based out of Kottayam. Kottayam boasts several other colleges and universities. It is also home to one of the world's most renowned institutes for Syriac studies: [St. Ephrem Ecumenical Research Institute](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Ephrem_Ecumenical_Research_Institute "St. Ephrem Ecumenical Research Institute").[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kottayam#cite_note-35)

There are 14 engineering colleges. Government Engineering College - [Rajiv Gandhi Institute of Technology, Kottayam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rajiv_Gandhi_Institute_of_Technology,_Kottayam "Rajiv Gandhi Institute of Technology, Kottayam") is located in Pampady, 14 km east of Kottayam. Indian institute of information technology, Kottayam, an institute of national importance is also located around 30 km (19 mi) from Kottayam, near to Pala town. [Indian Institute of Mass Communication](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Institute_of_Mass_Communication "Indian Institute of Mass Communication") (IIMC) has one of its regional centres near Pampady, Kottayam.

## Media

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kottayam&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Media")]

In 1821, [Benjamin Bailey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benjamin_Bailey_(missionary) "Benjamin Bailey (missionary)"), a British missionary, established C.M.S. Press, the first printing press in Kerala, in Kottayam. The town has been at the forefront of newspaper and book publishing in the state ever since.

Newspaper _[Malayala Manorama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malayala\_Manorama "Malayala Manorama"),_ published from Kottayam, is one of the largest circulating dailies in India.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kottayam#cite_note-36) The Malayala Manorama Group, based in Kottayam, also owns Manorama Online, Manorama News Channel, _[The Week](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Week\_(Indian\_magazine) "The Week (Indian magazine)")_ magazine and other publications. Other major Malayalam newspapers—_[Mathrubhoomi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mathrubhoomi "Mathrubhoomi"),_ _[Deshabhimani](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deshabhimani "Deshabhimani"),_ _[Deepika](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deepika\_(newspaper) "Deepika (newspaper)"),_ _[Madhyamam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madhyamam "Madhyamam"),_ and around thirty periodicals are published from Kottayam. Kottayam is also home to several Malayalam book publishers such as [D.C. Books](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/D._C._Books "D. C. Books"), [Labour India Publications](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Labour_India_Publications "Labour India Publications") and Current Books. Almost 70 percent of books published in Kerala are from Kottayam.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kottayam#cite_note-37) In 1945, a group of writers set up [Sahithya Pravarthaka Sahakarana Sangham](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sahithya_Pravarthaka_Co-operative_Society "Sahithya Pravarthaka Co-operative Society") (English: Literary Workers' Co-operative Society) in Malayalam.

### Sports

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kottayam&action=edit&section=12 "Edit section: Sports")]

A number of annual basketball tournaments, including the Marian Trophy, Girideepam Trophy, Lourdes Trophy, and Virginia Memorial Tournament, are conducted in Kottayam. The main sports stadiums in Kottayam are Nehru Stadium and Rajiv Gandhi Indoor Stadium, both located in Nagambadom. Native Ball (നാടൻ പന്തുകളി) is also a well-known traditional sport in the region.

### Legislature

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kottayam&action=edit&section=14 "Edit section: Legislature")]

Kottayam is one of the six municipalities in the district, formed after the implementation of the Kerala Municipalities Act in 1994. The members of the municipal council are elected from each of the 52 wards every five years, coinciding with the local government elections across the state. The chairperson is the executive authority of the municipality.

Kottayam city is the part of the Kottayam legislative assembly constituency and the [Kottayam Lok Sabha constituency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kottayam_(Lok_Sabha_constituency) "Kottayam (Lok Sabha constituency)"). The legislative assembly election is conducted every four years, last in May 2016.

### Executive

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kottayam&action=edit&section=15 "Edit section: Executive")]

[![Image 15](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/1d/KottayamCollectorate.jpg/250px-KottayamCollectorate.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:KottayamCollectorate.jpg)

Kottayam Collectorate

The [collectorate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Collectorate "Collectorate") of the [Kottayam District](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kottayam_District "Kottayam District") is located in Kottayam city. The present collector is Sri. Chetan Kumar Meena IAS. Shri.S.Sreejith IAS serves as Additional District Magistrate and Deputy Collector (General) of Kottayam District.

Many administrative and district offices of Kottayam including the District Court is situated within the collectorate premises.

### Judiciary

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kottayam&action=edit&section=16 "Edit section: Judiciary")]

Five courts were established during the tenure of [Colonel John Munro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Munro,_9th_of_Teaninich "John Munro, 9th of Teaninich"), as the Diwan of various states in India. One of these was established in [Vaikom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vaikom "Vaikom"), in the northwest of Kottayam district.

The district court at Kottayam was established in 1910 during the period of [Sree Moolam Thirunal Maharaja of Travancore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moolam_Thirunal "Moolam Thirunal"). The court celebrated its centenary in 2010.

The District Headquarters of the judiciary is set up at Kottayam city with the Principal District Court as its administrative centre. The justice delivery system consists of eight [Munsiff Courts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Munsiff_court?action=edit&redlink=1 "Munsiff court (page does not exist)"), ten Judicial First Class Magistrate Courts, three Sub Courts, one Chief Judicial Magistrate Court, and three Additional District Courts. In addition to these regular courts, two Motor Accidents Claims Tribunals, one special court for Vigilance cases, and two Family Courts also function in the district.

## Politics

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kottayam&action=edit&section=17 "Edit section: Politics")]

[![Image 16](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/8e/Thiruvanchoor_Radhakrishnan.jpg/250px-Thiruvanchoor_Radhakrishnan.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Thiruvanchoor_Radhakrishnan.jpg)

[Thiruvanchoor Radhakrishnan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvanchoor_Radhakrishnan "Thiruvanchoor Radhakrishnan"), The current member of legislative assembly (MLA) from Kottayam

The major political parties active in Kottayam are [Indian National Congress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_National_Congress "Indian National Congress") (INC), [Communist Party of India (Marxist)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Communist_Party_of_India_(Marxist) "Communist Party of India (Marxist)") (CPI(M)), [Bharatiya Janata Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bharatiya_Janata_Party "Bharatiya Janata Party") (BJP) and [Kerala Congress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kerala_Congress "Kerala Congress"). Trade union movements are also popular in Kottayam as [Bharatiya Mazdoor Sangh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bharatiya_Mazdoor_Sangh "Bharatiya Mazdoor Sangh") (BMS, Indian Workers' Union), [Indian National Trade Union Congress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_National_Trade_Union_Congress "Indian National Trade Union Congress") (INTUC) and [Centre of Indian Trade Unions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Centre_of_Indian_Trade_Unions "Centre of Indian Trade Unions") (CITU) affiliated workers engaged in the labor sector.

The current municipal chairperson is M.P Santhoshkumar and vice-chairperson is Sheeba Punnen. [United Democratic Front (Kerala)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Democratic_Front_(Kerala) "United Democratic Front (Kerala)") (UDF[K]) is the ruling coalition of parties, holding a majority in the municipal council.

The current member of the legislative assembly (MLA) from Kottayam is [Thiruvanchoor Radhakrishnan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvanchoor_Radhakrishnan "Thiruvanchoor Radhakrishnan"),[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kottayam#cite_note-39) who has been representing the Kottayam town constituency since 2011.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kottayam#cite_note-40)

He is also the current Speaker of the [Kerala Legislative Assembly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kerala_Legislative_Assembly "Kerala Legislative Assembly").

**Kottayam Lok Sabha constituency** is one of the 20 [Lok Sabha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lok_Sabha "Lok Sabha") (parliamentary) constituencies in [Kerala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kerala "Kerala") state in southern [India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/India "India").

**Kilimanoor** is a panchayat and a town in the [Chirayinkeezhu taluk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chirayinkeezhu_taluk "Chirayinkeezhu taluk") of [Thiruvananthapuram district](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_district "Thiruvananthapuram district") in [Kerala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kerala "Kerala"), India.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kilimanoor#cite_note-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kilimanoor#cite_note-2) It is located on [MC/SH 1 Road](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Main_central_Road "Main central Road"), 33 kilometres (21 mi) northwest of the city of Thiruvananthapuram ([Trivandrum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trivandrum "Trivandrum")), 14 km (8.7 mi) east of [Attingal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Attingal "Attingal") and 20 km (12 mi) east of [Varkala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Varkala "Varkala").

## History

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kilimanoor&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]

Kilimanoor ("land of the bird and the deer") was ruled by a [Pillai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sai_pillai_meleputhiyakav_(Kerala_title)?action=edit&redlink=1 "Sai pillai meleputhiyakav (Kerala title) (page does not exist)") ruling chief and was forfeited to Travancore by Maharaja Marthanda Varma. The estate comprising several villages was then handed over to the family of the father of the King who had come south from Parappanad in Malabar around 1718.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kilimanoor#cite_note-3) was ruled by a chief during time of the [Ettuveetil Pillamar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ettuveetil_Pillamar "Ettuveetil Pillamar") in the kingdom of [Travancore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Travancore "Travancore"). The chief rebelled against the [Maharajah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maharajah "Maharajah")[Marthanda Varma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marthanda_Varma "Marthanda Varma"), and the region was annexed and later given to the Royal House of Kilimanoor.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kilimanoor#cite_note-FOOTNOTEAiya1906329-4)

This [Royal House of Kilimanoor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_House_of_Kilimanoor "Royal House of Kilimanoor") has a history of more than 300 years. In 1705 (ME 880), the son and two daughters of Ittammar Raja of Beypore Thattarikovilakam, a [Parappanad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parappanad "Parappanad") royal house, were adopted by the Royal house of [Venad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Venad "Venad"). Parappanad was actually the ruling family of [Parappanangadi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parappanangadi "Parappanangadi") in present-day [Malappuram district](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malappuram_district "Malappuram district"). Ittammar Raja's sister and her sons, Rama Varma and Raghava Varma, settled in Kilimanoor and married the now-adopted sisters. Marthanda Varma, the founder of the [Kingdom of Travancore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kingdom_of_Travancore "Kingdom of Travancore") was the son of Raghava Varma. Raghava Varma's nephew, Ravi Varma Koil Thampuran, married Marthanda Varma's sister. Their son came to be known as Dharma Raja Kartika Thirunnal Rama Varma. In 1740, when an allied force led by Dutch Captain Hockert supporting the Deshinganadu king attacked Venad, an army from Kilimanoor tactfully resisted and then defeated them. Although a small victory, this was the first time an Indian army defeated a European power. In recognition of this feat, Marthanda Varma, in 1753, exempted the areas under control of [Kilimanoor Palace](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kilimanoor_Palace "Kilimanoor Palace") from taxes and proclaimed autonomous status. The present palace complex was also built during this time along with the Ayyappa temple for the family deity.

Velu Thampi Dalawa held meetings at the Kilimanoor Palace, planning his revolts against the [British](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Raj "British Raj"). He handed over his sword at the palace before going for his final battle against the British. India's First President, [Dr. Rajendra Prasad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dr._Rajendra_Prasad "Dr. Rajendra Prasad") received the sword from the palace, and it is now kept at the [National Museum, New Delhi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Museum,_New_Delhi "National Museum, New Delhi"). Subsequently, placed at the Napier Museum in the capital city of Kerala.

## Transportation

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kilimanoor&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Transportation")]

Kilimanoor is on the [Main Central Road](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Main_Central_Road "Main Central Road"). It is connected to the whole major destination by buses run by [KSRTC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kerala_State_Road_Transport_Corporation "Kerala State Road Transport Corporation") from the Kilimanoor bus depot. Kilimanoor is only 33 kilometres (21 mi) away from [Thiruvananthapuram](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram "Thiruvananthapuram"). The nearest airport is [Trivandrum International Airport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trivandrum_International_Airport "Trivandrum International Airport"). The nearest major railway station is [Varkala Railway Station](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Varkala_Railway_Station "Varkala Railway Station") which is 20 km (12 mi) from Kilimanoor.

**Kilimanoor** is a panchayat and a town in the [Chirayinkeezhu taluk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chirayinkeezhu_taluk "Chirayinkeezhu taluk") of [Thiruvananthapuram district](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_district "Thiruvananthapuram district") in [Kerala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kerala "Kerala"), India.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kilimanoor#cite_note-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kilimanoor#cite_note-2) It is located on [MC/SH 1 Road](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Main_central_Road "Main central Road"), 33 kilometres (21 mi) northwest of the city of Thiruvananthapuram ([Trivandrum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trivandrum "Trivandrum")), 14 km (8.7 mi) east of [Attingal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Attingal "Attingal") and 20 km (12 mi) east of [Varkala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Varkala "Varkala").

## History

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kilimanoor&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]

Kilimanoor ("land of the bird and the deer") was ruled by a [Pillai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sai_pillai_meleputhiyakav_(Kerala_title)?action=edit&redlink=1 "Sai pillai meleputhiyakav (Kerala title) (page does not exist)") ruling chief and was forfeited to Travancore by Maharaja Marthanda Varma. The estate comprising several villages was then handed over to the family of the father of the King who had come south from Parappanad in Malabar around 1718.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kilimanoor#cite_note-3) was ruled by a chief during time of the [Ettuveetil Pillamar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ettuveetil_Pillamar "Ettuveetil Pillamar") in the kingdom of [Travancore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Travancore "Travancore"). The chief rebelled against the [Maharajah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maharajah "Maharajah")[Marthanda Varma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marthanda_Varma "Marthanda Varma"), and the region was annexed and later given to the Royal House of Kilimanoor.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kilimanoor#cite_note-FOOTNOTEAiya1906329-4)

This [Royal House of Kilimanoor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_House_of_Kilimanoor "Royal House of Kilimanoor") has a history of more than 300 years. In 1705 (ME 880), the son and two daughters of Ittammar Raja of Beypore Thattarikovilakam, a [Parappanad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parappanad "Parappanad") royal house, were adopted by the Royal house of [Venad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Venad "Venad"). Parappanad was actually the ruling family of [Parappanangadi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parappanangadi "Parappanangadi") in present-day [Malappuram district](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malappuram_district "Malappuram district"). Ittammar Raja's sister and her sons, Rama Varma and Raghava Varma, settled in Kilimanoor and married the now-adopted sisters. Marthanda Varma, the founder of the [Kingdom of Travancore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kingdom_of_Travancore "Kingdom of Travancore") was the son of Raghava Varma. Raghava Varma's nephew, Ravi Varma Koil Thampuran, married Marthanda Varma's sister. Their son came to be known as Dharma Raja Kartika Thirunnal Rama Varma. In 1740, when an allied force led by Dutch Captain Hockert supporting the Deshinganadu king attacked Venad, an army from Kilimanoor tactfully resisted and then defeated them. Although a small victory, this was the first time an Indian army defeated a European power. In recognition of this feat, Marthanda Varma, in 1753, exempted the areas under control of [Kilimanoor Palace](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kilimanoor_Palace "Kilimanoor Palace") from taxes and proclaimed autonomous status. The present palace complex was also built during this time along with the Ayyappa temple for the family deity.

Velu Thampi Dalawa held meetings at the Kilimanoor Palace, planning his revolts against the [British](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Raj "British Raj"). He handed over his sword at the palace before going for his final battle against the British. India's First President, [Dr. Rajendra Prasad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dr._Rajendra_Prasad "Dr. Rajendra Prasad") received the sword from the palace, and it is now kept at the [National Museum, New Delhi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Museum,_New_Delhi "National Museum, New Delhi"). Subsequently, placed at the Napier Museum in the capital city of Kerala.

## Transportation

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kilimanoor&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Transportation")]

Kilimanoor is on the [Main Central Road](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Main_Central_Road "Main Central Road"). It is connected to the whole major destination by buses run by [KSRTC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kerala_State_Road_Transport_Corporation "Kerala State Road Transport Corporation") from the Kilimanoor bus depot. Kilimanoor is only 33 kilometres (21 mi) away from [Thiruvananthapuram](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram "Thiruvananthapuram"). The nearest airport is [Trivandrum International Airport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trivandrum_International_Airport "Trivandrum International Airport"). The nearest major railway station is [Varkala Railway Station](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Varkala_Railway_Station "Varkala Railway Station") which is 20 km (12 mi) from Kilimanoor.

**Ramanathapuram** ([pronunciation](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/transcoded/4/40/Ramanathapuram.ogg/Ramanathapuram.ogg.mp3 "Play audio")[ⓘ](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Ramanathapuram.ogg "File:Ramanathapuram.ogg")), also known as **Ramnad**,[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ramanathapuram#cite_note-ramnad-1) is a town in [Ramanathapuram district](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ramanathapuram_district "Ramanathapuram district") in the [Indian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/India "India")[state](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/States_and_territories_of_India "States and territories of India") of [Tamil Nadu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tamil_Nadu "Tamil Nadu"). It is the administrative headquarters of [Ramanathapuram district](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ramanathapuram_district "Ramanathapuram district") and the second largest town (by population) in Ramanathapuram district.

## History

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Ramanathapuram&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]

[![Image 8](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/db/The_temple_of_Ramnad%2C_South_India_%28XV%2C_August_1858%2C_p.84%29_-_Copy.jpg/330px-The_temple_of_Ramnad%2C_South_India_%28XV%2C_August_1858%2C_p.84%29_-_Copy.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:The_temple_of_Ramnad,_South_India_(XV,_August_1858,_p.84)_-_Copy.jpg)

The temple of Mugavai, South India (1858)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ramanathapuram#cite_note-Offering1858-2)

See also: [Ramnad estate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ramnad_estate "Ramnad estate")

The town is at times referred to as Mukhavai (Mugavai) Nagaram, that is, Entrance town.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ramanathapuram#cite_note-:0-3) The region is well known since Puranic ages. The estate of Ramnad included the Hindu holy island city of [Rameswaram](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rameswaram "Rameswaram"), from where, legend has it that the Hindu god [Rama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rama "Rama") launched his invasion of [Ravana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ravana "Ravana")'s [Lanka](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lanka "Lanka"). On the conclusion of the war and Rama's success in it, he appointed a _Sethupathi_ or "lord of the bridge" to guard the way to the island. The "bridge" referred to here is a chain of natural [limestone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Limestone "Limestone")[shoals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shoal "Shoal") known as [Adam's Bridge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adam's_Bridge "Adam's Bridge"),[[a]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ramanathapuram#cite_note-4) also known as **Rama's Bridge** or _**Rama Setu**_,[[b]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ramanathapuram#cite_note-5) which according to Hindu legend is believed to have been constructed by Rama. The chieftains of Ramnad were entrusted with the responsibility of protecting the bridge, hence the appellation.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

Historically, for a short period, this area had been under the [Chola dynasty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chola_dynasty "Chola dynasty") when [Rajendra Chola I](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rajendra_Chola_I "Rajendra Chola I") brought it under his territory in 1063 CE.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

In the late 12th and early 13th centuries, this province was ruled by Hazrat Sulthan Syed Ibrahim shaheed of [Ervadi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ervadi "Ervadi"). Later on, his heirs were ruling the province following a peace treaty with the Sethupathis. From then, until the early 15th century the present territories of [Ramanathapuram district](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ramanathapuram_district "Ramanathapuram district")—comprising the _[taluks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tehsil "Tehsil")_[Tiruvadanai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tiruvadanai "Tiruvadanai"), [Kilakarai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kilakarai "Kilakarai"), [Paramakudi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paramakudi "Paramakudi"), [Kamuthi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kamuthi "Kamuthi"), [Mudukulathur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mudukulathur "Mudukulathur"), Ramanathapuram and [Rameswaram](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rameswaram "Rameswaram")—were included in the [Pandyan Empire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pandyan_dynasty "Pandyan dynasty").[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

During the 14th and 15th centuries, the traditional chieftain of the region who belonged to the [Maravar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mukkulathor#Maravar "Mukkulathor") caste was officially recognized as _Sethupathi_ by the [Nayak king of Madurai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madurai_Nayaks "Madurai Nayaks"). The chieftain of Ramnad, in return, recognized the sovereignty of the Nayak king over his lands. When the power of the Nayak kings of [Madurai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madurai "Madurai") began to decline in the late 17th century, the chieftains of Ramnad asserted their independence. In the late 17th century, Raghunatha Kilavan crowned himself king of Ramnad and changed his seat from Pogalur to Ramnad close to the east coast. He erected massive fortifications to protect his capital. In 1725, the [king of Tanjore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thanjavur_Marathas "Thanjavur Marathas") claimed the northern part of the Ramnad kingdom (the [Aranthangi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aranthangi "Aranthangi") region) up to the river Pambar in return for his services during the civil war in Ramnad. A vassal of Ramnad who was amongst the victors in the civil war took over the westerly located [Sivaganga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sivaganga "Sivaganga") region, thereby leaving only three-fifths of the kingdom actually in the hands of the king of Ramnad. At the beginning of the 18th century, family disputes over succession resulted in the division of Ramanathapuram. With the help of the King of Thanjavur in 1730, one of the chieftains deposed the Sethupathi and became the Raja of Sivaganga.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

In 1741 the area came under the control of the Marathas and then under the Nizam in 1744. Dissatisfied with the Nawab's rule, the chieftains revolted, led by the last ruling Nayak, against the Nawab in 1752. By that time, the throne of Arcot had two rivals, [Chanda Shahib](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chanda_Shahib "Chanda Shahib") and [Muhammed Ali](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Muhammed_Ali_Khan_Wallajah "Muhammed Ali Khan Wallajah"), and this district was under the rule of Nawab of Arcot. The British supported Chand Sahib, whilst the French supported Muhammed Ali. This paved the way for a series of conflicts in the southern part of the continent also called [Carnatic Wars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carnatic_Wars "Carnatic Wars").

In 1795, the British deposed Muthuramalinga Sethupathi and took control of the administration of Ramanathapuram. After the death of the Queen [Velu Nachiyar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Velu_Nachiyar "Velu Nachiyar"), the [Maruthu brothers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maruthu_Pandiyar "Maruthu Pandiyar") took charge by paying regular revenue to the East India company. In 1803 the Maruthu Pandiyar of [Sivaganga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sivaganga "Sivaganga") revolted against the British in collaboration with Kattabomman of Panchalamkurichi. Colonel Agnew captured and hanged the Maruthu brothers. After the fall of [Tippu Sultan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tippu_Sultan "Tippu Sultan"), the British took control and imprisoned the Nawab. In 1892 the Zamindari system was abolished and a British collector was appointed for administration.

In 1910, Ramanathapuram was formed from portions of [Madurai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madurai_district "Madurai district") and [Tirunelveli districts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tirunelveli_district "Tirunelveli district"), with J.F. Bryant as the first collector. During the British period this district was called "Ramnad"; the name continued after independence. Later the district was renamed as Ramanathapuram to be in conformity with the Tamil name for this region."Ramnad" is also known as "Mugavai"(face) since it acts as the entry point for River "[Vaigai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vaigai_River "Vaigai River")".[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

According to [2011 census](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_census_of_India "2011 census of India"), Ramanathapuram had a population of 61,440 with a sex-ratio of 988 females for every 1,000 males, much above the national average of 929.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ramanathapuram#cite_note-dashboard-6) A total of 6,370 were under the age of six, constituting 3,245 males and 3,125 females. The average literacy of the town was 93.42%, compared to the national average of 72.99%.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ramanathapuram#cite_note-dashboard-6) The town had a total of 14716 households. There were a total of 20,375 workers, comprising 115 cultivators, 178 main agricultural labourers, 262 in house hold industries, 18,773 other workers, 1,047 marginal workers, 20 marginal cultivators, 30 marginal agricultural labourers, 41 marginal workers in household industries and 956 other marginal workers.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ramanathapuram#cite_note-2011census-7)

Among Hindus [Agamudayars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Agamudayars "Agamudayars"), [Maravars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maravars "Maravars"),[Kallars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kallars "Kallars"), [Konars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Konar_(caste) "Konar (caste)"), [Devendrakulam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Devendrakulam "Devendrakulam") are more predominant population and also large number of [Vellalars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vellalars "Vellalars"), [Muslims](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Muslims "Muslims") constitute a demographic population in Ramanathapuram District.

As per the religious census of 2011, Ramanathapuram had 76.39% [Hindus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hindus "Hindus"), 19.77% [Muslims](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Muslims "Muslims"), 3.08% [Christians](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christians "Christians"), 0.01% [Sikhs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sikhs "Sikhs"), 0.7% following other religions and 0.01% following no religion or did not indicate any religious preference.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ramanathapuram#cite_note-religion2011-8)

## Civic administration

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Ramanathapuram&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Civic administration")]

Ramanathapuram is a municipality. After shifting the district headquarters' offices from Madurai to Ramanathapuram, the town is growing. The gauge conversion of the railway from Madurai to Rameswaram and from [Trichy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trichy "Trichy") to Rameswaram connects the town to all major Indian cities. Ramanathapuram district was a larger district in Tamil Nadu, and later some of its portions were removed to create Sivaganga district.

The river Vaigai enters the _Big Tank_ (periya kanmaai) and the water is collected for the purpose of agriculture. It is claimed that the river water does not reach the sea, portraying the size of the catchment area. The town has many ponds catering to the needs of the populace. It is a good sign to have few engineering colleges like Anna University, UCER-Ramnad campus, Syed Ammal Engineering College and Mohamed Sathak Engineering College.

Former Indian president [A.P.J. Abdul Kalam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A.P.J._Abdul_Kalam "A.P.J. Abdul Kalam") attended Schwartz Higher Secondary School, Ramanathapuram.

## Geography

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Ramanathapuram&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Geography")]

Ramanathapuram is located at [9°23′N 78°50′E / 9.38°N 78.83°E / 9.38; 78.83](https://geohack.toolforge.org/geohack.php?pagename=Ramanathapuram&params=9.38_N_78.83_E_).[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ramanathapuram#cite_note-9) It has an average elevation of 2 metres (6 feet). The nearest towns include [Paramakudi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paramakudi "Paramakudi"), [Rameshwaram](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rameshwaram "Rameshwaram"), [Mudukulathur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mudukulathur "Mudukulathur"), [Kilakarai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kilakarai "Kilakarai") and [Manamadurai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manamadurai "Manamadurai").

## Transport

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Ramanathapuram&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Transport")]

The town is located in south east Tamil Nadu and connected by [NH 49](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Highway_49_(India) "National Highway 49 (India)") (also called as [AH 43](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AH43 "AH43")) to Madurai from Rameswaram. [East Coast Road](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_Coast_Road "East Coast Road") is the major coastal road in east [Tamil Nadu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tamil_Nadu "Tamil Nadu") which connects the state capital Chennai and Ramanathapuram; this road also connects Ramanathapuram with [Pondicherry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pondicherry_(city) "Pondicherry (city)"), [Thoothukudi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thoothukudi "Thoothukudi") and Kanyakumari. [Ramanathapuram railway station](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ramanathapuram_railway_station "Ramanathapuram railway station") is well connected by railroad to major cities in India through [Madurai Junction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madurai_Junction "Madurai Junction") and [Karaikudi Junction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karaikudi_Junction "Karaikudi Junction").

The nearest international airport is [Madurai Airport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madurai_Airport "Madurai Airport"), about 125 km and domestic airport is [Tuticorin Airport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tuticorin_Airport "Tuticorin Airport") about 140 km. The Nearest Naval Station is located in [Uchipuli](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uchipuli "Uchipuli") In the name of [INS Parundu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/INS_Parundu "INS Parundu").

## Tourism

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Ramanathapuram&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Tourism")]

[![Image 9](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/7c/Ramanathapuram_Palace_Outside.jpg/250px-Ramanathapuram_Palace_Outside.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Ramanathapuram_Palace_Outside.jpg)

Palace of Ramanathapuram

Tourists visit Ramnad to see the Raja Palace,[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ramanathapuram#cite_note-11) still occupied by the former Sethupaty Raja and his family.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

The royal family sends the elephant for Santhanakoodu procession in [Erwadi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Erwadi "Erwadi") during the annual [Santhanakoodu Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Erwadi_Santhanakoodu_Festival "Erwadi Santhanakoodu Festival").

Ramanathapuram is close to [Rameswaram](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rameswaram "Rameswaram"), [Devipattinam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Devipattinam "Devipattinam"), [Thiruppullani](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adi_Jagannatha_Perumal_Temple "Adi Jagannatha Perumal Temple"), and [Uthirakosamangai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uthirakosamangai "Uthirakosamangai") which are very important ancient pilgrimage centres.

[Uchipuli](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uchipuli "Uchipuli"), an Indian naval air station with near by Ariyamaan Beach is one among the popular beaches in Uchipuli.

[Periyapattinam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Periyapattinam "Periyapattinam"), [Athiyuthu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Athiyuthu "Athiyuthu"), [Panaikulam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Panaikulam "Panaikulam"), [Alagankulam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alagankulam "Alagankulam"), [Puduvalasai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Puduvalasai?action=edit&redlink=1 "Puduvalasai (page does not exist)"), Chittarkottai, [Valoor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Valoor?action=edit&redlink=1 "Valoor (page does not exist)") beaches are other popular in Ramnad region.

And there is also memorial for former President of India [A. P. J. Abdul Kalam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A._P._J._Abdul_Kalam "A. P. J. Abdul Kalam") is also located at Peikarumbu near Ramanathapuram.

**Ramanathapuram** ([pronunciation](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/transcoded/4/40/Ramanathapuram.ogg/Ramanathapuram.ogg.mp3 "Play audio")[ⓘ](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Ramanathapuram.ogg "File:Ramanathapuram.ogg")), also known as **Ramnad**,[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ramanathapuram#cite_note-ramnad-1) is a town in [Ramanathapuram district](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ramanathapuram_district "Ramanathapuram district") in the [Indian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/India "India")[state](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/States_and_territories_of_India "States and territories of India") of [Tamil Nadu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tamil_Nadu "Tamil Nadu"). It is the administrative headquarters of [Ramanathapuram district](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ramanathapuram_district "Ramanathapuram district") and the second largest town (by population) in Ramanathapuram district.

## History

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Ramanathapuram&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]

[![Image 8](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/db/The_temple_of_Ramnad%2C_South_India_%28XV%2C_August_1858%2C_p.84%29_-_Copy.jpg/330px-The_temple_of_Ramnad%2C_South_India_%28XV%2C_August_1858%2C_p.84%29_-_Copy.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:The_temple_of_Ramnad,_South_India_(XV,_August_1858,_p.84)_-_Copy.jpg)

The temple of Mugavai, South India (1858)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ramanathapuram#cite_note-Offering1858-2)

See also: [Ramnad estate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ramnad_estate "Ramnad estate")

The town is at times referred to as Mukhavai (Mugavai) Nagaram, that is, Entrance town.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ramanathapuram#cite_note-:0-3) The region is well known since Puranic ages. The estate of Ramnad included the Hindu holy island city of [Rameswaram](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rameswaram "Rameswaram"), from where, legend has it that the Hindu god [Rama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rama "Rama") launched his invasion of [Ravana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ravana "Ravana")'s [Lanka](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lanka "Lanka"). On the conclusion of the war and Rama's success in it, he appointed a _Sethupathi_ or "lord of the bridge" to guard the way to the island. The "bridge" referred to here is a chain of natural [limestone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Limestone "Limestone")[shoals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shoal "Shoal") known as [Adam's Bridge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adam's_Bridge "Adam's Bridge"),[[a]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ramanathapuram#cite_note-4) also known as **Rama's Bridge** or _**Rama Setu**_,[[b]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ramanathapuram#cite_note-5) which according to Hindu legend is believed to have been constructed by Rama. The chieftains of Ramnad were entrusted with the responsibility of protecting the bridge, hence the appellation.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

Historically, for a short period, this area had been under the [Chola dynasty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chola_dynasty "Chola dynasty") when [Rajendra Chola I](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rajendra_Chola_I "Rajendra Chola I") brought it under his territory in 1063 CE.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

In the late 12th and early 13th centuries, this province was ruled by Hazrat Sulthan Syed Ibrahim shaheed of [Ervadi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ervadi "Ervadi"). Later on, his heirs were ruling the province following a peace treaty with the Sethupathis. From then, until the early 15th century the present territories of [Ramanathapuram district](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ramanathapuram_district "Ramanathapuram district")—comprising the _[taluks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tehsil "Tehsil")_[Tiruvadanai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tiruvadanai "Tiruvadanai"), [Kilakarai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kilakarai "Kilakarai"), [Paramakudi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paramakudi "Paramakudi"), [Kamuthi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kamuthi "Kamuthi"), [Mudukulathur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mudukulathur "Mudukulathur"), Ramanathapuram and [Rameswaram](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rameswaram "Rameswaram")—were included in the [Pandyan Empire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pandyan_dynasty "Pandyan dynasty").[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

During the 14th and 15th centuries, the traditional chieftain of the region who belonged to the [Maravar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mukkulathor#Maravar "Mukkulathor") caste was officially recognized as _Sethupathi_ by the [Nayak king of Madurai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madurai_Nayaks "Madurai Nayaks"). The chieftain of Ramnad, in return, recognized the sovereignty of the Nayak king over his lands. When the power of the Nayak kings of [Madurai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madurai "Madurai") began to decline in the late 17th century, the chieftains of Ramnad asserted their independence. In the late 17th century, Raghunatha Kilavan crowned himself king of Ramnad and changed his seat from Pogalur to Ramnad close to the east coast. He erected massive fortifications to protect his capital. In 1725, the [king of Tanjore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thanjavur_Marathas "Thanjavur Marathas") claimed the northern part of the Ramnad kingdom (the [Aranthangi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aranthangi "Aranthangi") region) up to the river Pambar in return for his services during the civil war in Ramnad. A vassal of Ramnad who was amongst the victors in the civil war took over the westerly located [Sivaganga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sivaganga "Sivaganga") region, thereby leaving only three-fifths of the kingdom actually in the hands of the king of Ramnad. At the beginning of the 18th century, family disputes over succession resulted in the division of Ramanathapuram. With the help of the King of Thanjavur in 1730, one of the chieftains deposed the Sethupathi and became the Raja of Sivaganga.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

In 1741 the area came under the control of the Marathas and then under the Nizam in 1744. Dissatisfied with the Nawab's rule, the chieftains revolted, led by the last ruling Nayak, against the Nawab in 1752. By that time, the throne of Arcot had two rivals, [Chanda Shahib](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chanda_Shahib "Chanda Shahib") and [Muhammed Ali](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Muhammed_Ali_Khan_Wallajah "Muhammed Ali Khan Wallajah"), and this district was under the rule of Nawab of Arcot. The British supported Chand Sahib, whilst the French supported Muhammed Ali. This paved the way for a series of conflicts in the southern part of the continent also called [Carnatic Wars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carnatic_Wars "Carnatic Wars").

In 1795, the British deposed Muthuramalinga Sethupathi and took control of the administration of Ramanathapuram. After the death of the Queen [Velu Nachiyar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Velu_Nachiyar "Velu Nachiyar"), the [Maruthu brothers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maruthu_Pandiyar "Maruthu Pandiyar") took charge by paying regular revenue to the East India company. In 1803 the Maruthu Pandiyar of [Sivaganga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sivaganga "Sivaganga") revolted against the British in collaboration with Kattabomman of Panchalamkurichi. Colonel Agnew captured and hanged the Maruthu brothers. After the fall of [Tippu Sultan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tippu_Sultan "Tippu Sultan"), the British took control and imprisoned the Nawab. In 1892 the Zamindari system was abolished and a British collector was appointed for administration.

In 1910, Ramanathapuram was formed from portions of [Madurai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madurai_district "Madurai district") and [Tirunelveli districts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tirunelveli_district "Tirunelveli district"), with J.F. Bryant as the first collector. During the British period this district was called "Ramnad"; the name continued after independence. Later the district was renamed as Ramanathapuram to be in conformity with the Tamil name for this region."Ramnad" is also known as "Mugavai"(face) since it acts as the entry point for River "[Vaigai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vaigai_River "Vaigai River")".[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

According to [2011 census](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_census_of_India "2011 census of India"), Ramanathapuram had a population of 61,440 with a sex-ratio of 988 females for every 1,000 males, much above the national average of 929.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ramanathapuram#cite_note-dashboard-6) A total of 6,370 were under the age of six, constituting 3,245 males and 3,125 females. The average literacy of the town was 93.42%, compared to the national average of 72.99%.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ramanathapuram#cite_note-dashboard-6) The town had a total of 14716 households. There were a total of 20,375 workers, comprising 115 cultivators, 178 main agricultural labourers, 262 in house hold industries, 18,773 other workers, 1,047 marginal workers, 20 marginal cultivators, 30 marginal agricultural labourers, 41 marginal workers in household industries and 956 other marginal workers.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ramanathapuram#cite_note-2011census-7)

Among Hindus [Agamudayars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Agamudayars "Agamudayars"), [Maravars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maravars "Maravars"),[Kallars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kallars "Kallars"), [Konars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Konar_(caste) "Konar (caste)"), [Devendrakulam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Devendrakulam "Devendrakulam") are more predominant population and also large number of [Vellalars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vellalars "Vellalars"), [Muslims](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Muslims "Muslims") constitute a demographic population in Ramanathapuram District.

As per the religious census of 2011, Ramanathapuram had 76.39% [Hindus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hindus "Hindus"), 19.77% [Muslims](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Muslims "Muslims"), 3.08% [Christians](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christians "Christians"), 0.01% [Sikhs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sikhs "Sikhs"), 0.7% following other religions and 0.01% following no religion or did not indicate any religious preference.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ramanathapuram#cite_note-religion2011-8)

## Civic administration

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Ramanathapuram&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Civic administration")]

Ramanathapuram is a municipality. After shifting the district headquarters' offices from Madurai to Ramanathapuram, the town is growing. The gauge conversion of the railway from Madurai to Rameswaram and from [Trichy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trichy "Trichy") to Rameswaram connects the town to all major Indian cities. Ramanathapuram district was a larger district in Tamil Nadu, and later some of its portions were removed to create Sivaganga district.

The river Vaigai enters the _Big Tank_ (periya kanmaai) and the water is collected for the purpose of agriculture. It is claimed that the river water does not reach the sea, portraying the size of the catchment area. The town has many ponds catering to the needs of the populace. It is a good sign to have few engineering colleges like Anna University, UCER-Ramnad campus, Syed Ammal Engineering College and Mohamed Sathak Engineering College.

Former Indian president [A.P.J. Abdul Kalam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A.P.J._Abdul_Kalam "A.P.J. Abdul Kalam") attended Schwartz Higher Secondary School, Ramanathapuram.

## Geography

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Ramanathapuram&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Geography")]

Ramanathapuram is located at [9°23′N 78°50′E / 9.38°N 78.83°E / 9.38; 78.83](https://geohack.toolforge.org/geohack.php?pagename=Ramanathapuram&params=9.38_N_78.83_E_).[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ramanathapuram#cite_note-9) It has an average elevation of 2 metres (6 feet). The nearest towns include [Paramakudi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paramakudi "Paramakudi"), [Rameshwaram](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rameshwaram "Rameshwaram"), [Mudukulathur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mudukulathur "Mudukulathur"), [Kilakarai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kilakarai "Kilakarai") and [Manamadurai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manamadurai "Manamadurai").

## Transport

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Ramanathapuram&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Transport")]

The town is located in south east Tamil Nadu and connected by [NH 49](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Highway_49_(India) "National Highway 49 (India)") (also called as [AH 43](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AH43 "AH43")) to Madurai from Rameswaram. [East Coast Road](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_Coast_Road "East Coast Road") is the major coastal road in east [Tamil Nadu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tamil_Nadu "Tamil Nadu") which connects the state capital Chennai and Ramanathapuram; this road also connects Ramanathapuram with [Pondicherry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pondicherry_(city) "Pondicherry (city)"), [Thoothukudi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thoothukudi "Thoothukudi") and Kanyakumari. [Ramanathapuram railway station](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ramanathapuram_railway_station "Ramanathapuram railway station") is well connected by railroad to major cities in India through [Madurai Junction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madurai_Junction "Madurai Junction") and [Karaikudi Junction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karaikudi_Junction "Karaikudi Junction").

The nearest international airport is [Madurai Airport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madurai_Airport "Madurai Airport"), about 125 km and domestic airport is [Tuticorin Airport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tuticorin_Airport "Tuticorin Airport") about 140 km. The Nearest Naval Station is located in [Uchipuli](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uchipuli "Uchipuli") In the name of [INS Parundu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/INS_Parundu "INS Parundu").

## Tourism

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Ramanathapuram&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Tourism")]

[![Image 9](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/7c/Ramanathapuram_Palace_Outside.jpg/250px-Ramanathapuram_Palace_Outside.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Ramanathapuram_Palace_Outside.jpg)

Palace of Ramanathapuram

Tourists visit Ramnad to see the Raja Palace,[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ramanathapuram#cite_note-11) still occupied by the former Sethupaty Raja and his family.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

The royal family sends the elephant for Santhanakoodu procession in [Erwadi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Erwadi "Erwadi") during the annual [Santhanakoodu Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Erwadi_Santhanakoodu_Festival "Erwadi Santhanakoodu Festival").

Ramanathapuram is close to [Rameswaram](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rameswaram "Rameswaram"), [Devipattinam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Devipattinam "Devipattinam"), [Thiruppullani](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adi_Jagannatha_Perumal_Temple "Adi Jagannatha Perumal Temple"), and [Uthirakosamangai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uthirakosamangai "Uthirakosamangai") which are very important ancient pilgrimage centres.

[Uchipuli](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uchipuli "Uchipuli"), an Indian naval air station with near by Ariyamaan Beach is one among the popular beaches in Uchipuli.

[Periyapattinam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Periyapattinam "Periyapattinam"), [Athiyuthu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Athiyuthu "Athiyuthu"), [Panaikulam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Panaikulam "Panaikulam"), [Alagankulam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alagankulam "Alagankulam"), [Puduvalasai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Puduvalasai?action=edit&redlink=1 "Puduvalasai (page does not exist)"), Chittarkottai, [Valoor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Valoor?action=edit&redlink=1 "Valoor (page does not exist)") beaches are other popular in Ramnad region.

And there is also memorial for former President of India [A. P. J. Abdul Kalam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A._P._J._Abdul_Kalam "A. P. J. Abdul Kalam") is also located at Peikarumbu near Ramanathapuram.

**[Thiruvananthapuram](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram "Thiruvananthapuram") Parliamentary (Lok Sabha) Constituency** is one of the 20 parliamentary constituencies in Kerala, India. It is located in [Thiruvananthapuram district](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_district "Thiruvananthapuram district") and encompasses the major part of [Thiruvananthapuram](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram "Thiruvananthapuram") city, the capital of [Kerala State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kerala "Kerala").

The incumbent MP of this constituency, [Shashi Tharoor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Tharoor "Shashi Tharoor") of the [Indian National Congress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_National_Congress "Indian National Congress"), has been elected on 4 consecutive occasions: 2009, 2014, 2019 and 2024. He is the longest serving Member of Parliament to have represented the constituency.

## Demographics

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Thiruvananthapuram_Lok_Sabha_constituency&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Demographics")]

This constituency is dominated By [Nair](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nair "Nair") and [Nadar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nadar_(caste) "Nadar (caste)").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_(Lok_Sabha_constituency)#cite_note-2) As per the electoral roll for the 2024 polls, the total electorate is of 14,03,281 people including 7,27,469 women, 6,75,771 men and 41 transgender people.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_(Lok_Sabha_constituency)#cite_note-3) Out of total electorate, 26% is rural and 74% is urban. The Scheduled castes (SC) and Scheduled tribes (ST) is 9.82% and 0.45%, respectively of total electorate.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_(Lok_Sabha_constituency)#cite_note-4) The constituency also has highest proportion of [Nadars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nadar_(caste) "Nadar (caste)") and [Converted Christians](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conversion_to_Christianity "Conversion to Christianity") in Kerala.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_(Lok_Sabha_constituency)#cite_note-5)[Nairs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nair "Nair") dominates the urban segments of [Kazhakootam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kazhakootam_Assembly_constituency "Kazhakootam Assembly constituency"),[Nemom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nemom_Assembly_constituency "Nemom Assembly constituency"),[Vattiyoorkavu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vattiyoorkavu_Assembly_constituency "Vattiyoorkavu Assembly constituency") and [Thiruvananthapuram](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_Assembly_constituency "Thiruvananthapuram Assembly constituency") While the [Nadars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nadar_(caste) "Nadar (caste)") are Concentrated on [Neyyattinkara](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neyyattinkara_Assembly_constituency "Neyyattinkara Assembly constituency"),[Parassala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parassala_Assembly_constituency "Parassala Assembly constituency"),[Kovalam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kovalam_Assembly_constituency "Kovalam Assembly constituency").

As per the voter list published by the Election commission for the 2019 Lok Sabha elections, there were 13,34,665 voters in the electorate and 1077 polling stations in this constituency.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_(Lok_Sabha_constituency)#cite_note-ceo.kerala.gov.in-6) The voter turnout for the 2019 Lok Sabha election was 73.45% where as it was 68.63% and 65.74% in the 2014 and 2009 elections respectively.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_(Lok_Sabha_constituency)#cite_note-7)

**[Thiruvananthapuram](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram "Thiruvananthapuram") Parliamentary (Lok Sabha) Constituency** is one of the 20 parliamentary constituencies in Kerala, India. It is located in [Thiruvananthapuram district](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_district "Thiruvananthapuram district") and encompasses the major part of [Thiruvananthapuram](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram "Thiruvananthapuram") city, the capital of [Kerala State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kerala "Kerala").

The incumbent MP of this constituency, [Shashi Tharoor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Tharoor "Shashi Tharoor") of the [Indian National Congress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_National_Congress "Indian National Congress"), has been elected on 4 consecutive occasions: 2009, 2014, 2019 and 2024. He is the longest serving Member of Parliament to have represented the constituency.

## Demographics

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Thiruvananthapuram_Lok_Sabha_constituency&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Demographics")]

This constituency is dominated By [Nair](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nair "Nair") and [Nadar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nadar_(caste) "Nadar (caste)").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_(Lok_Sabha_constituency)#cite_note-2) As per the electoral roll for the 2024 polls, the total electorate is of 14,03,281 people including 7,27,469 women, 6,75,771 men and 41 transgender people.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_(Lok_Sabha_constituency)#cite_note-3) Out of total electorate, 26% is rural and 74% is urban. The Scheduled castes (SC) and Scheduled tribes (ST) is 9.82% and 0.45%, respectively of total electorate.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_(Lok_Sabha_constituency)#cite_note-4) The constituency also has highest proportion of [Nadars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nadar_(caste) "Nadar (caste)") and [Converted Christians](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conversion_to_Christianity "Conversion to Christianity") in Kerala.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_(Lok_Sabha_constituency)#cite_note-5)[Nairs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nair "Nair") dominates the urban segments of [Kazhakootam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kazhakootam_Assembly_constituency "Kazhakootam Assembly constituency"),[Nemom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nemom_Assembly_constituency "Nemom Assembly constituency"),[Vattiyoorkavu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vattiyoorkavu_Assembly_constituency "Vattiyoorkavu Assembly constituency") and [Thiruvananthapuram](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_Assembly_constituency "Thiruvananthapuram Assembly constituency") While the [Nadars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nadar_(caste) "Nadar (caste)") are Concentrated on [Neyyattinkara](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neyyattinkara_Assembly_constituency "Neyyattinkara Assembly constituency"),[Parassala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parassala_Assembly_constituency "Parassala Assembly constituency"),[Kovalam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kovalam_Assembly_constituency "Kovalam Assembly constituency").

As per the voter list published by the Election commission for the 2019 Lok Sabha elections, there were 13,34,665 voters in the electorate and 1077 polling stations in this constituency.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_(Lok_Sabha_constituency)#cite_note-ceo.kerala.gov.in-6) The voter turnout for the 2019 Lok Sabha election was 73.45% where as it was 68.63% and 65.74% in the 2014 and 2009 elections respectively.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_(Lok_Sabha_constituency)#cite_note-7)
