**Kottayam district** (IPA:[[koːʈːɐjɐm]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/Malayalam "Help:IPA/Malayalam")[](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/transcoded/4/45/LL-Q36236_%28mal%29-Vis_M-%E0%B4%95%E0%B5%8B%E0%B4%9F%E0%B5%8D%E0%B4%9F%E0%B4%AF%E0%B4%82.wav/LL-Q36236_%28mal%29-Vis_M-%E0%B4%95%E0%B5%8B%E0%B4%9F%E0%B5%8D%E0%B4%9F%E0%B4%AF%E0%B4%82.wav.mp3 "Play audio")[ⓘ](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:LL-Q36236_(mal)-Vis_M-%E0%B4%95%E0%B5%8B%E0%B4%9F%E0%B5%8D%E0%B4%9F%E0%B4%AF%E0%B4%82.wav "File:LL-Q36236 (mal)-Vis M-കോട്ടയം.wav")) is one of [14 districts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_districts_of_Kerala "List of districts of Kerala") in the [Indian state](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/States_and_union_territories_of_India "States and union territories of India") of [Kerala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kerala "Kerala").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kottayam_district#cite_note-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kottayam_district#cite_note-5) Kottayam district comprises six municipal towns: Kottayam, [Changanassery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Changanassery "Changanassery"), [Pala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pala,_Kerala "Pala, Kerala"), [Erattupetta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Erattupetta "Erattupetta"), [Ettumanoor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ettumanoor "Ettumanoor"), and [Vaikom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vaikom "Vaikom"). Situated in the central part of Kerala, Kottayam shares its borders with Ernakulam, Idukki, Pathanamthitta, and Alappuzha districts. It is the only [district](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_districts_in_India "List of districts in India") in Kerala that does not border either the Arabian Sea or another Indian state.

The district is bordered by hills in the east, and the [Vembanad Lake](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vembanad_Lake "Vembanad Lake") and [paddy fields](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paddy_field "Paddy field") of [Kuttanad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kuttanad "Kuttanad") on the west. The area's geographic features include paddy fields, highlands, and hills. As of the 2011 census, 28.6% of the district's residents live in urban areas, and it reports a 97.2% [literacy rate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Literacy_in_India "Literacy in India").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kottayam_district#cite_note-6) In 2008, the district became the first tobacco-free district in India.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kottayam_district#cite_note-7) Kottayam registered the lowest [Multidimensional Poverty Index](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Multidimensional_Poverty_Index "Multidimensional Poverty Index") (MPI) of zero among all districts of India, indicating no deprivation as per the report published by [Oxford Poverty and Human Development Initiative](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oxford_Poverty_and_Human_Development_Initiative "Oxford Poverty and Human Development Initiative") and [UNDP](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UNDP "UNDP") for districts across India.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kottayam_district#cite_note-8) The district's headquarters are based in the city of Kottayam.

[Hindustan Newsprint Limited](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hindustan_Newsprint_Limited "Hindustan Newsprint Limited") and [Rubber Board](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rubber_Board "Rubber Board") are two central government organizations located in the district. The headquarters of two religious communities in Kerala are also in the Kottayam District: [Nair Service Society](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nair_Service_Society "Nair Service Society") and the [Indian Orthodox Church](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Orthodox_Church "Indian Orthodox Church").

## Etymology

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kottayam_district&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Etymology")]

The name Kottayam is a combination of the words "kotta" and "akam" in the local language of [Malayalam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malayalam "Malayalam"), meaning "interior of a fort".[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kottayam_district#cite_note-9)

## History

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kottayam_district&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: History")]

See also: [History of Kerala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_Kerala "History of Kerala")

### Prehistoric period

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kottayam_district&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Prehistoric period")]

Main article: [Prehistory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prehistory "Prehistory")

A substantial portion of Kottayam district may have been under the [Arabian Sea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arabian_Sea "Arabian Sea") during prehistoric times. Marine fossils have been found in an area near [Changanassery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Changanassery "Changanassery"), thus supporting the hypothesis.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kottayam_district#cite_note-feudal_states_in_early_18th_century_Kerala-10)

However, there are archaeological evidences of the early human inhabitation period of this district, including ancient fossils, stone inscriptions and monuments, in the archeological sites like the excavation sites, the caves, the temples, etc. The literary works of the [Sangam period](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sangam_period "Sangam period") also help to take a look into the ancient period of the district.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kottayam_district#cite_note-feudal_states_in_early_18th_century_Kerala-10)

### Classical Antiquity

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kottayam_district&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Classical Antiquity")]

Main article: [Classical Antiquity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Classical_Antiquity "Classical Antiquity")

#### Chera dynasty and the Keralaputras of ancient Tamilakam (up to 5th century CE)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kottayam_district&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Chera dynasty and the Keralaputras of ancient Tamilakam (up to 5th century CE)")]

Main article: [Chera dynasty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chera_dynasty "Chera dynasty")

See also: [Tamilakam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tamilakam "Tamilakam")

[![Image 15](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/2f/Chera_country_%28early_historic_south_India%29.jpg/250px-Chera_country_%28early_historic_south_India%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Chera_country_(early_historic_south_India).jpg)

The extent of the [Chera dynasty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chera_dynasty "Chera dynasty") (known as _Keralaputras_ in the inscriptions of the emperor [Ashoka](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashoka "Ashoka") of the [Maurya Empire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maurya_Empire "Maurya Empire") (322 [BCE](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Before_Common_Era "Before Common Era") – 184 BCE)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kottayam_district#cite_note-feudal_states_in_early_18th_century_Kerala-10) during the early centuries of the [Common Era](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Common_Era "Common Era").

Early members of the [Chera dynasty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chera_dynasty "Chera dynasty") (first few centuries of the [Common Era](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Common_Era "Common Era")) had their original headquarters in a region called _Kuzhamur_ at _Kuttanad_ in the ancient [Tamilakam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tamilakam "Tamilakam") and were sometimes known as the _Kuttuvans_.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kottayam_district#cite_note-feudal_states_in_early_18th_century_Kerala-10) The [Chera dynasty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chera_dynasty "Chera dynasty") is mentioned as _Keralaputras_ in the inscriptions of the emperor [Ashoka](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashoka "Ashoka") of the [Maurya Empire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maurya_Empire "Maurya Empire") (322 [BCE](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Before_Common_Era "Before Common Era") – 184 BCE).[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kottayam_district#cite_note-feudal_states_in_early_18th_century_Kerala-10)

The province _Kuttanad_ of the ancient kingdom of _Keralaputras_ included the modern-day districts of Kottayam, [Ernakulam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ernakulam_district "Ernakulam district"), [Idukki](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Idukki_district "Idukki district"), and parts of [Alappuzha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alappuzha_district "Alappuzha district"), which can be defined as the region between the rivers [Periyar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Periyar_river "Periyar river") and [Pamba](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pamba_River "Pamba River").[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kottayam_district#cite_note-feudal_states_in_early_18th_century_Kerala-10) It was bounded by the [Ay kingdom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ay_kingdom "Ay kingdom") to the south, which included the regions between [Pamba River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pamba_River "Pamba River") and [Kanyakumari](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kanyakumari "Kanyakumari") (Cape Comorin), and the province of _Kudanad_, which lies between the rivers [Periyar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Periyar_river "Periyar river") and [Chaliyar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chaliyar_river "Chaliyar river") (modern-day districts of [Thrissur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thrissur_district "Thrissur district"), [Palakkad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palakkad_district "Palakkad district"), and [Malappuram](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malappuram_district "Malappuram district")), to the north.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kottayam_district#cite_note-feudal_states_in_early_18th_century_Kerala-10)

It was during the reign of [Uthiyan Cheralathan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uthiyan_Cheralathan "Uthiyan Cheralathan") (105–130 CE) that the [Chera dynasty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chera_dynasty "Chera dynasty") began to expand towards the northern and the eastern regions of _Kuttanad_ by conquering the provinces of _Kudanadu_ and _[Kongu Nadu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kongu\_Nadu "Kongu Nadu")_.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kottayam_district#cite_note-feudal_states_in_early_18th_century_Kerala-10) Afterwards the dynasty got split into three branches and fixed their capitals at [Muziris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Muziris "Muziris"), [Tyndis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tyndis "Tyndis"), and [Caroura](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karur "Karur"), respectively, as seen in the ancient [Greco-Roman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greco-Roman_world "Greco-Roman world") travelogues as well as the [Old Tamil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Old_Tamil "Old Tamil") literary works of the [Sangam period](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sangam_period "Sangam period").[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kottayam_district#cite_note-feudal_states_in_early_18th_century_Kerala-10) During the reign of _Narmudi Cheral_, the regions included in the [Kingdom of Ezhimala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mushika_dynasty "Mushika dynasty") was also added to the Chera empire.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kottayam_district#cite_note-feudal_states_in_early_18th_century_Kerala-10)

#### Invasions and social transformation from 6th century CE to 800 CE

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kottayam_district&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Invasions and social transformation from 6th century CE to 800 CE")]

See also: [Kalabhra dynasty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kalabhra_dynasty "Kalabhra dynasty"), [Pallava dynasty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pallava_dynasty "Pallava dynasty"), [Chalukya dynasty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chalukya_dynasty "Chalukya dynasty"), [Pandya dynasty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pandya_dynasty "Pandya dynasty"), and [Rashtrakuta dynasty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rashtrakuta_dynasty "Rashtrakuta dynasty")

The ancient Chera empire collapsed due to the continuous invasions carried out by the [Kalabhras](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kalabhra_dynasty "Kalabhra dynasty"), the [Pallavas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pallava_dynasty "Pallava dynasty"), the [Chalukyas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chalukya_dynasty "Chalukya dynasty"), the [Pandyas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pandya_dynasty "Pandya dynasty"), and the [Rashtrakutas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rashtrakuta_dynasty "Rashtrakuta dynasty") during the period between 500 CE and 800 CE for nearly three centuries.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kottayam_district#cite_note-feudal_states_in_early_18th_century_Kerala-10) This era marked the migration of [Nambudiri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nambudiri "Nambudiri")[Brahmins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brahmin "Brahmin") into the district, which later led to a transformation in the social structure of the region after the 10th century CE.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kottayam_district#cite_note-feudal_states_in_early_18th_century_Kerala-10) The ancient prominent religions in the district like [Buddhism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Buddhism "Buddhism") began to vanish after the 10th century CE. [Sri Mulavasam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sri_Mulavasam "Sri Mulavasam") was a prominent centre of [Buddhism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Buddhism "Buddhism") in the [Indian peninsula](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_peninsula "Indian peninsula") until the early medieval period, prior to the Chera-Chola wars of the 11th century CE.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kottayam_district#cite_note-feudal_states_in_early_18th_century_Kerala-10)

### Medieval history

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kottayam_district&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Medieval history")]

The regions included in the modern-day district of Kottayam is described well in the medieval Kerala literature which includes works written in both [Malayalam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malayalam "Malayalam") and [Sanskrit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sanskrit "Sanskrit").[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kottayam_district#cite_note-feudal_states_in_early_18th_century_Kerala-10) The 14th century [Sanskrit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sanskrit "Sanskrit") work _Sukasandesam_ describes about [Kaduthuruthy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kaduthuruthy "Kaduthuruthy").[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kottayam_district#cite_note-feudal_states_in_early_18th_century_Kerala-10) Similarly the 17th century Sanskrit work _Bhramara Sandesam_ contains details about [Kumaranalloor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kumaranalloor "Kumaranalloor") and [Vaikom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vaikom "Vaikom").[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kottayam_district#cite_note-feudal_states_in_early_18th_century_Kerala-10) The 18th century Sanskrit literary work _Chathaka Sandesam_ also contains references to [Vaikom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vaikom "Vaikom").[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kottayam_district#cite_note-feudal_states_in_early_18th_century_Kerala-10)

_[Unnuneeli Sandesam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unnuneeli\_Sandesam "Unnuneeli Sandesam")_, a work which belongs to the [Malayalam literature](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malayalam_literature "Malayalam literature") written during early decades of the 14th century CE, contains a short geographical and political description of the regions and the medieval [feudal states](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Feudalism "Feudalism") that lied between [Kaduthuruthy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kaduthuruthy "Kaduthuruthy") and Thiruvananthapuram.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kottayam_district#cite_note-feudal_states_in_early_18th_century_Kerala-10) It contains details about the medieval kingdoms of [Thekkumkur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thekkumkur "Thekkumkur") (1102–1749) and [Vadakkumkur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vadakkumkur "Vadakkumkur") (1102–1750) those together constitute the modern district of Kottayam.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kottayam_district#cite_note-feudal_states_in_early_18th_century_Kerala-10)

The writings and the records of the [Portuguese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portuguese_India "Portuguese India") as well as the [Dutch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dutch_Malabar "Dutch Malabar"), who visited and interfered in the political affairs of the district after the [Age of Discovery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Age_of_Discovery "Age of Discovery") (1498 CE), such as the _[Hortus Malabaricus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hortus\_Malabaricus "Hortus Malabaricus")_, contain significant information about the geographical and the political conditions of the region during the late medieval period.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kottayam_district#cite_note-feudal_states_in_early_18th_century_Kerala-10)

#### The Chera Perumals of Mahodayapuram (800 – 1102 CE)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kottayam_district&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: The Chera Perumals of Mahodayapuram (800 – 1102 CE)")]

Main article: [Chera Perumals of Makotai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chera_Perumals_of_Makotai "Chera Perumals of Makotai")

See also: [Vazhappally copper plate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vazhappally_copper_plate "Vazhappally copper plate")

See also: [Medieval Cholas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Medieval_Cholas "Medieval Cholas")

[![Image 16](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/80/South_India_in_early_11th_century_AD.jpg/250px-South_India_in_early_11th_century_AD.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:South_India_in_early_11th_century_AD.jpg)

[Kerala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kerala "Kerala") during 11th century CE (the region which is marked as _Chera_)

The area included in the modern-day district of Kottayam was part of three _Nadus_ (provinces) during the period of the [Chera Perumals of Mahodayapuram](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chera_Perumals_of_Makotai "Chera Perumals of Makotai") (800–1102 [CE](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Common_Era "Common Era")) for nearly three centuries.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kottayam_district#cite_note-feudal_states_in_early_18th_century_Kerala-10) The region around the city of Kottayam was known as _Munjunadu_, while the [Vaikom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vaikom "Vaikom")-[Meenachil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meenachil "Meenachil") region, which lies to the north of _Munjunadu_ was included in a province called _Vempolinadu_ (known as _Bimbali Desam_ in Sanskrit).[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kottayam_district#cite_note-feudal_states_in_early_18th_century_Kerala-10) The third province was the _Nantuzhainadu_ which constitutes the modern-day [Taluks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_taluks_of_Kerala "List of taluks of Kerala") of [Changanassery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Changanassery "Changanassery") and [Thiruvalla](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvalla "Thiruvalla").[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kottayam_district#cite_note-feudal_states_in_early_18th_century_Kerala-10) This period saw the decline of [Buddhism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Buddhism "Buddhism") and [Jainism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jainism "Jainism"), which were once prominent in the region, along with the growth of [Hinduism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hinduism "Hinduism") characterised by a large-scale migration of the [Nambudiri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nambudiri "Nambudiri")[Brahmins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brahmin "Brahmin") into the region.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kottayam_district#cite_note-feudal_states_in_early_18th_century_Kerala-10)

The territory of the Chera Perumals of Mahodayapuram disintegrated into several small [feudal states](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Feudalism "Feudalism") by early 12th century CE as a result of the continuous war that occurred between the Chera Perumals and the [Medieval Cholas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Medieval_Cholas "Medieval Cholas") throughout the 11th century CE.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kottayam_district#cite_note-feudal_states_in_early_18th_century_Kerala-10)

[![Image 17](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/8e/Vazhappally_copper_plate_%289th_century_AD%29.jpg/250px-Vazhappally_copper_plate_%289th_century_AD%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Vazhappally_copper_plate_(9th_century_AD).jpg)

The [Vazhappally copper plate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vazhappally_copper_plate "Vazhappally copper plate") (882/883 CE) written in [Old Malayalam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Old_Malayalam "Old Malayalam"), found near [Changanassery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Changanassery "Changanassery").[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kottayam_district#cite_note-feudal_states_in_early_18th_century_Kerala-10)

The [Vazhappally copper plate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vazhappally_copper_plate "Vazhappally copper plate") (c. 882/83 CE[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kottayam_district#cite_note-:28-11)) is a copper plate inscription written in [Old Malayalam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Old_Malayalam "Old Malayalam") language that dates back to the 9th century CE found at [Vazhappally](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vazhappally "Vazhappally") in Kottayam district.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kottayam_district#cite_note-:12-12)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kottayam_district#cite_note-:02-13) Recent scholarship puts the date of the plate in c. 882/83 CE.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kottayam_district#cite_note-:3-14) The inscription is engraved on a single copper plate (with five lines on both sides) in an early form of the [Old Malayalam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Old_Malayalam "Old Malayalam") language in [Vatteluttu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vatteluttu "Vatteluttu") script with some [Grantha characters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grantha_script "Grantha script"). The contents of the plate are incomplete.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kottayam_district#cite_note-:12-12) The inscription was discovered by V. Srinivasa Sastri from _Thalamana Illam_ near [Changanassery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Changanassery "Changanassery").[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kottayam_district#cite_note-:23-15) The plate is owned by _Muvidathu Madom_, [Thiruvalla](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvalla "Thiruvalla").[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kottayam_district#cite_note-:12-12) The record is dated to the twelfth [regnal year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Regnal_year "Regnal year") of Chera Perumal king [Rama Rajasekhara](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rajashekhara_(Chera_king) "Rajashekhara (Chera king)") (882/83 CE).[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kottayam_district#cite_note-:3-14)

[![Image 18](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/55/Perunna_inscription_of_Rama_Kulasekhara_%281099_AD%29.jpg/250px-Perunna_inscription_of_Rama_Kulasekhara_%281099_AD%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Perunna_inscription_of_Rama_Kulasekhara_(1099_AD).jpg)

The [Perunna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Perunna "Perunna") inscription (1099 CE) of [Rama Kulasekhara](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rama_Kulasekhara "Rama Kulasekhara") written in [Old Malayalam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Old_Malayalam "Old Malayalam"), found near [Changanassery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Changanassery "Changanassery").[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kottayam_district#cite_note-:9-16)

Inscriptions related to [Rama Kulasekhara](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rama_Kulasekhara "Rama Kulasekhara") (1089–1123 CE) of Chera Perumal dynasty can be found at [Perunna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Perunna "Perunna") near [Changanassery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Changanassery "Changanassery").[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kottayam_district#cite_note-:35-17) The [Perunna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Perunna "Perunna") inscription dates back to the year 1099 CE (the 10th regional year of Rama Kulasekhara).[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kottayam_district#cite_note-:9-16)

#### Thekkumkur dynasty (1102–1749 CE)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kottayam_district&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Thekkumkur dynasty (1102–1749 CE)")]

Main article: [Thekkumkur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thekkumkur "Thekkumkur")

See also: [Battle of Changanassery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Changanassery "Battle of Changanassery")

[![Image 19](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/4e/Map_of_Thekkumkur_in_1790.jpg/250px-Map_of_Thekkumkur_in_1790.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Map_of_Thekkumkur_in_1790.jpg)

A political map of the Kingdom of [Thekkumkur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thekkumkur "Thekkumkur") (1102–1749)

The province _Vempolinadu_ (_Bimbali Desam_) of the Chera Perumals of Mahodayapuram attained political autonomy in 1102 CE following the Chera-Chola wars of the 11th century CE.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kottayam_district#cite_note-feudal_states_in_early_18th_century_Kerala-10) The _Vempolinadu_ royal family got evolved into two independent branches by the 12th century CE – the southern branch among them later came to be known as the kingdom of [Thekkumkur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thekkumkur "Thekkumkur").[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kottayam_district#cite_note-feudal_states_in_early_18th_century_Kerala-10) It included the modern-day [Taluks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_taluks_of_Kerala "List of taluks of Kerala") of [Changanassery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Changanassery "Changanassery"), [Kanjirappally](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kanjirappally "Kanjirappally"), Kottayam, and [Thiruvalla](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvalla "Thiruvalla").[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kottayam_district#cite_note-feudal_states_in_early_18th_century_Kerala-10) The kings of the Thekkumkur dynasty are described by the titles _Bimbaleeshas_ and _Manikandas_ in the Sanskrit literary works.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kottayam_district#cite_note-feudal_states_in_early_18th_century_Kerala-10)[Vennimala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vennimala "Vennimala") and [Manikandapuram](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manikandapuram "Manikandapuram") were the early headquarters of the Thekkumkur dynasty.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kottayam_district#cite_note-feudal_states_in_early_18th_century_Kerala-10) Later it was transferred to [Thazhathangady](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thazhathangady_Juma_Mosque "Thazhathangady Juma Mosque") near the town of Kottayam.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kottayam_district#cite_note-feudal_states_in_early_18th_century_Kerala-10) Thazhathangady is one of the places in Kerala where a church, a mosque, and a Hindu temple co-exist together, which points out the religious harmony that existed under the _Thekkumkur Rajas_. At times, the town of [Changanassery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Changanassery "Changanassery") acted as headquarters of the Thekkumkur dynasty.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kottayam_district#cite_note-feudal_states_in_early_18th_century_Kerala-10)

The _Thekkumkur Rajas_ were vassals to the [Kingdom of Cochin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kingdom_of_Cochin "Kingdom of Cochin") until the mid-18th century CE.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kottayam_district#cite_note-feudal_states_in_early_18th_century_Kerala-10) Thekkumkur Rajas also allied with the [Kingdom of Cochin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kingdom_of_Cochin "Kingdom of Cochin") and the Kingdom of [Odanad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Odanad "Odanad") ([Kayamkulam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kayamkulam "Kayamkulam")) against the military invasions of the kingdom of [Travancore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Travancore "Travancore") into its northern kingdoms that occurred during the 1740s.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kottayam_district#cite_note-feudal_states_in_early_18th_century_Kerala-10) As a result, Anizham Thirunal [Marthanda Varma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marthanda_Varma "Marthanda Varma"), the architect of the modern Travancore, attacked and annexed the kingdom of [Thekkumkur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thekkumkur "Thekkumkur") into Travancore in 1749 during the [Battle of Changanassery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Changanassery "Battle of Changanassery"), after his annexation of [Kayamkulam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kayamkulam "Kayamkulam") in 1746.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kottayam_district#cite_note-feudal_states_in_early_18th_century_Kerala-10) The Thekkumkur king took refuge in the kingdom of the [Zamorin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zamorin "Zamorin") of Calicut following his defeat in the battle.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kottayam_district#cite_note-feudal_states_in_early_18th_century_Kerala-10)

#### Vadakkumkur dynasty (1102–1750 CE)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kottayam_district&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Vadakkumkur dynasty (1102–1750 CE)")]

Main article: [Vadakkumkur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vadakkumkur "Vadakkumkur")

[Vadakkumkur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vadakkumkur "Vadakkumkur") was the northern branch of the erstwhile province of _Vempolinadu_ which attained political autonomy in 1102 CE after the collapse of the Chera Perumals of Mahodayapuram.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kottayam_district#cite_note-feudal_states_in_early_18th_century_Kerala-10) The rulers of this dynasty were also known by the titles _Bimbaleeshas_ and _Manikandas_ in the contemporary Sanskrit works just like their [Thekkumkur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thekkumkur "Thekkumkur") counterparts. The kingdom of [Vadakkumkur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vadakkumkur "Vadakkumkur") included the modern-day Taluks of [Ettumanoor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ettumanoor "Ettumanoor") and [Vaikom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vaikom "Vaikom") along with a portion of the [Meenachil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meenachil "Meenachil") Taluk.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kottayam_district#cite_note-feudal_states_in_early_18th_century_Kerala-10)[Kaduthuruthy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kaduthuruthy "Kaduthuruthy") was the earlier headquarters of the [Vadakkumkur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vadakkumkur "Vadakkumkur") dynasty which was later transferred into [Vaikom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vaikom "Vaikom").[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kottayam_district#cite_note-feudal_states_in_early_18th_century_Kerala-10) Vadakkumkur was a vassal state of the [Kingdom of Cochin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kingdom_of_Cochin "Kingdom of Cochin") until 1750.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kottayam_district#cite_note-feudal_states_in_early_18th_century_Kerala-10)

The [Portuguese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portuguese_India "Portuguese India") explorers described [Vadakkumkur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vadakkumkur "Vadakkumkur") as "The Pepper country" due to the availability and high scale production of good quality pepper there during the 16th century CE.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kottayam_district#cite_note-feudal_states_in_early_18th_century_Kerala-10) The [Dutch Malabar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dutch_Malabar "Dutch Malabar") who became an influential power in the territory of Vadakkumkur during the 17th century CE and the first half of the 18th century CE had a trade centre at [Vechoor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vechoor "Vechoor") (in [Vaikom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vaikom "Vaikom")[taluk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_taluks_of_Kerala "List of taluks of Kerala")) in Vadakkumkur.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kottayam_district#cite_note-feudal_states_in_early_18th_century_Kerala-10) The Kingdom of _Kizhmalanadu_ (1102–1600), which had included the modern-day Taluks of [Muvattupuzha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Muvattupuzha "Muvattupuzha") and [Thodupuzha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thodupuzha "Thodupuzha") with its headquarters at Karikode near Thodupuzha, merged with the kingdom of [Vadakkumkur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vadakkumkur "Vadakkumkur") around 1600 CE.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kottayam_district#cite_note-feudal_states_in_early_18th_century_Kerala-10)

[Vadakkumkur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vadakkumkur "Vadakkumkur") Raja was also a part of the combined military alliance formed by the kingdoms of [Odanad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Odanad "Odanad") (Kayamkulam), [Thekkumkur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thekkumkur "Thekkumkur"), and [Cochin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kingdom_of_Cochin "Kingdom of Cochin") against the expansion of [Travancore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Travancore "Travancore") into the northern territories.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kottayam_district#cite_note-feudal_states_in_early_18th_century_Kerala-10) As a result, Anizham Thirunal [Marthanda Varma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marthanda_Varma "Marthanda Varma"), the architect of the modern Travancore, attacked and annexed Vadakkumkur in 1750.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kottayam_district#cite_note-feudal_states_in_early_18th_century_Kerala-10) The Vadakkumkur Raja sought asylum in the kingdom of the [Zamorin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zamorin "Zamorin") of Calicut.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kottayam_district#cite_note-feudal_states_in_early_18th_century_Kerala-10) Later he returned back into Travancore.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kottayam_district#cite_note-feudal_states_in_early_18th_century_Kerala-10)

#### Poonjar dynasty (1160–1750 CE)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kottayam_district&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Poonjar dynasty (1160–1750 CE)")]

Main article: [Poonjar dynasty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Poonjar_dynasty "Poonjar dynasty")

In 1157 CE, [Kulothunga Chola](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kulothunga_I "Kulothunga I"), who belonged to the lineage of the [Medieval Cholas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Medieval_Cholas "Medieval Cholas"), entered into a war with Manavikrama Kulasekhara Perumal, who belonged to the [Pandya dynasty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pandya_dynasty "Pandya dynasty") of [Madurai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madurai "Madurai").[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kottayam_district#cite_note-feudal_states_in_early_18th_century_Kerala-10) Upon the failure in the battle, Manavikrama appointed his brother Maravarman Sreevallabha as the monarch of the [Pandya dynasty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pandya_dynasty "Pandya dynasty") and left Madurai with his family and some of his trusted servants.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kottayam_district#cite_note-feudal_states_in_early_18th_century_Kerala-10) Manavikrama crossed the [Western Ghats](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Western_Ghats "Western Ghats") and sought political asylum in [Kerala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kerala "Kerala").[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kottayam_district#cite_note-feudal_states_in_early_18th_century_Kerala-10) Manavikrama purchased a vast tract of land bordering the Pandyan territories, from the ruler of [Thekkumkur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thekkumkur "Thekkumkur") which comprised the [Meenachil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meenachil "Meenachil") taluk the regions of [Poonjar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Poonjar "Poonjar"), Erattupeta, Pala, Patthanamthitta, Thodupuzha, etc. along with the [High Range](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/High_Range,_Kerala "High Range, Kerala") region of modern-day [Idukki district](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Idukki_district "Idukki district") in 1160 CE, which originally belonged to the [Thekkumkur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thekkumkur "Thekkumkur") Rajas.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kottayam_district#cite_note-feudal_states_in_early_18th_century_Kerala-10) This incident commenced the beginning of the [Poonjar dynasty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Poonjar_dynasty "Poonjar dynasty"). They were a sovereign state.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kottayam_district#cite_note-feudal_states_in_early_18th_century_Kerala-10) Though disputed, the territory of Poonjar was claimed by the Kingdom of [Travancore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Travancore "Travancore") in 1899 AD. Travancore claimed that the sovereignty reverted to them following the annexation of the principalities of [Thekkumkur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thekkumkur "Thekkumkur") and [Vadakkumkur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vadakkumkur "Vadakkumkur") in 1749–1750.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kottayam_district#cite_note-feudal_states_in_early_18th_century_Kerala-10) The land ownership was not disputed.

The [Kannan Devan Hills](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kannan_Devan_Hills "Kannan Devan Hills") on the [High Range](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/High_Range,_Kerala "High Range, Kerala") region were given on lease on 11 July 1877 by the ruler of the [Poonjar dynasty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Poonjar_dynasty "Poonjar dynasty") to John Daniel Munroe from London and for [tea plantations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_tea_in_India "History of tea in India"). The land and the plantations were later resumed by the [Government of Kerala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Government_of_Kerala "Government of Kerala") through the Kannan Devan Hills (Resumption Of Lands) Act, 1971.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kottayam_district#cite_note-18) However, the act only addressed the issue of sovereignty which was taken over by the State of Kerala with the accession of Travancore to the Union of India. The ownership of the Kannan Devan plantation (125000 acres)leased to John Monroe, and subsequently transferred to Tata Finlay, and finally to Tata Tea was not relinquished by the Poonjar royal family. This was established by a court challenge to the status, which was resolved by a Kerala High Court order in the early 1990s. The order was in favor of the Poonjar royal family establishing ownership. The lease terms are currently being fulfilled with regards to lease payments as per the original deed.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

### Progress and Social Reformation during the Travancore era (1750–1947)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kottayam_district&action=edit&section=12 "Edit section: Progress and Social Reformation during the Travancore era (1750–1947)")]

Main article: [Travancore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Travancore "Travancore")

See also: [Kerala reformation movement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kerala_reformation_movement "Kerala reformation movement") and [Vaikom Satyagraha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vaikom_Satyagraha "Vaikom Satyagraha")

[![Image 20](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/63/Cms_college_old_building.JPG/250px-Cms_college_old_building.JPG?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Cms_college_old_building.JPG)

The [CMS College Kottayam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CMS_College_Kottayam "CMS College Kottayam"), established in 1815, was the first [Western model](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Western_world "Western world") institute of higher education in India.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kottayam_district#cite_note-feudal_states_in_early_18th_century_Kerala-10)

[![Image 21](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/c7/Travancore_1871.JPG/250px-Travancore_1871.JPG?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Travancore_1871.JPG)

A map of the [British](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Raj "British Raj")[princely state](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Princely_state "Princely state") of [Travancore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Travancore "Travancore") published in 1871

Entire portion of the modern-day district of Kottayam became part of the erstwhile [British](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Raj "British Raj")[princely state](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Princely_state "Princely state") of [Travancore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Travancore "Travancore") by 1750 CE. This era marked considerable progress and social reformation in all spheres.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kottayam_district#cite_note-feudal_states_in_early_18th_century_Kerala-10)

The [Church Mission Society](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Church_Mission_Society "Church Mission Society") press at Kottayam was established in 1821 by Rev. [Benjamin Baily](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benjamin_Bailey_(missionary) "Benjamin Bailey (missionary)"), a British missionary, as the first printing press in [Kerala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kerala "Kerala").[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kottayam_district#cite_note-19) They had also established the [CMS College Kottayam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CMS_College_Kottayam "CMS College Kottayam") in 1815 as the first [Western style](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Western_world "Western world") institute of higher education in India. The region progressed much in its literacy rate by the end of the 19th century CE.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kottayam_district#cite_note-feudal_states_in_early_18th_century_Kerala-10) It became one of the most literate regions in the [British Indian Empire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Raj "British Raj") by 1860.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kottayam_district#cite_note-feudal_states_in_early_18th_century_Kerala-10) Due to its remarkable progress in the fields of literacy, education, and printing, many early newspapers and magazines in [Malayalam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malayalam "Malayalam") such as _[Deepika](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deepika\_(newspaper) "Deepika (newspaper)")_ (1887) and _[Malayala Manorama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malayala\_Manorama "Malayala Manorama")_ (1888) were established in Kottayam.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kottayam_district#cite_note-feudal_states_in_early_18th_century_Kerala-10)

The same period also saw the commencement of [Kerala reformation movement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kerala_reformation_movement "Kerala reformation movement") with an aim to eradicate the [Untouchability](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Untouchability "Untouchability"), inequality, and the irrational practices existed in the Kerala society for many centuries which ultimately led to the movements like the [Vaikom Satyagraha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vaikom_Satyagraha "Vaikom Satyagraha") (1924).[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kottayam_district#cite_note-feudal_states_in_early_18th_century_Kerala-10) Kottayam has been involved in a number of political movements, including the 'Malayali Memorial' movement.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kottayam_district#cite_note-feudal_states_in_early_18th_century_Kerala-10) The goal of the movement was to seek more representation for [Malayalis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malayali "Malayali") in the [Travancore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Travancore "Travancore") civil service irrespective of their caste and religion.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kottayam_district#cite_note-:0-20)

[Vaikom Satyagraha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vaikom_Satyagraha "Vaikom Satyagraha"), a protest against [caste discrimination](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Caste_system_in_India "Caste system in India"), took place in Kottayam district in 1924.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kottayam_district#cite_note-feudal_states_in_early_18th_century_Kerala-10) The district also participated in the protests for responsible government in Travancore, which ended with the overthrow of [Sir C. P. Ramaswami Iyer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sir_C._P._Ramaswami_Iyer "Sir C. P. Ramaswami Iyer"), who was the [Divan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Divan "Divan") of the British princely state of Travancore in 1947.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kottayam_district#cite_note-feudal_states_in_early_18th_century_Kerala-10)

During the [Travancorean](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Travancore "Travancore") administration, the [British](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Raj "British Raj")[princely state](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Princely_state "Princely state") of Travancore was divided into four revenue divisions- the [Northern division](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Northern_Division_(Travancore) "Northern Division (Travancore)") headquartered at Kottayam, the [Central division](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Division_(Travancore) "Central Division (Travancore)") headquartered at [Kollam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kollam "Kollam"), the [Southern division](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southern_Division_(Travancore) "Southern Division (Travancore)") headquartered at Thiruvananthapuram, and the [High Range division](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/High_Range,_Kerala "High Range, Kerala") with its headquarters at [Devikulam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Devikulam "Devikulam").[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kottayam_district#cite_note-1931_census-21)

Kottayam was the headquarters of the northernmost revenue division in Travancore which included the [Taluks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_taluks_of_Kerala "List of taluks of Kerala") of [North Paravur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North_Paravur "North Paravur"), [Kunnathunad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kunnathunad "Kunnathunad"), [Muvattupuzha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Muvattupuzha "Muvattupuzha"), [Thodupuzha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thodupuzha "Thodupuzha"), [Meenachil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meenachil "Meenachil"), [Changanassery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Changanassery "Changanassery"), Kottayam, [Vaikom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vaikom "Vaikom"), and [Cherthala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cherthala "Cherthala") in 1931.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kottayam_district#cite_note-1931_census-21)

### Post-independence (1947–present)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kottayam_district&action=edit&section=13 "Edit section: Post-independence (1947–present)")]

See also: [Indian Independence Act 1947](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Independence_Act_1947 "Indian Independence Act 1947") and [Instrument of Accession](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Instrument_of_Accession "Instrument of Accession")

At the time of the integration of the state of [Travancore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Travancore "Travancore") and [Cochin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kingdom_of_Cochin "Kingdom of Cochin") into the state of [Travancore-Cochin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Travancore-Cochin "Travancore-Cochin") in 1949 following the integration of the [British](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Raj "British Raj")[Princely states](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Princely_state "Princely state") of [Travancore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Travancore "Travancore") and [Cochin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kingdom_of_Cochin "Kingdom of Cochin") into the [Dominion of India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominion_of_India "Dominion of India"), the erstwhile revenue divisions were reorganised into [districts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_districts_of_Kerala "List of districts of Kerala") and the [Divan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Divan "Divan") Peshkars gave way to [district collectors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/District_collector "District collector"), paving the way for the birth of the Kottayam district on 1 July 1949.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kottayam_district#cite_note-22)

The erstwhile [Kingdom of Cochin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kingdom_of_Cochin "Kingdom of Cochin") was reorganized into [Thrissur district](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thrissur_district "Thrissur district") and Taluks of [North Paravur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North_Paravur "North Paravur") and [Kunnathunad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kunnathunad "Kunnathunad") were transferred to that district.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kottayam_district#cite_note-1951c-23) Similarly the [Cherthala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cherthala "Cherthala") Taluk was transferred into the newly formed [Kollam district](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kollam_district "Kollam district") on 1 July 1949.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kottayam_district#cite_note-1951c-23) The [High Range](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/High_Range,_Kerala "High Range, Kerala") division of the erstwhile Travancore was merged with the remaining Taluks of the erstwhile Kottayam division to form the Kottayam district as a part of the inauguration of the new Indian state of [Travancore-Cochin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Travancore-Cochin "Travancore-Cochin") on 1 July 1949.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kottayam_district#cite_note-1951c-23) The new district of Kottayam at that time contained eight Taluks – Changanassery, Kottayam, Vaikom, Meenachil, Muvattupuzha, Thodupuzha, Devikulam, and Peerumede.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kottayam_district#cite_note-1951c-23)

As a part of the formation of the new Indian state of [Kerala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kerala "Kerala") according to the [States Reorganisation Act, 1956](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/States_Reorganisation_Act,_1956 "States Reorganisation Act, 1956"), many jurisdictional changes were done in the district.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kottayam_district#cite_note-1961c-24) Two new Taluks, namely [Kanjirappally](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kanjirappally "Kanjirappally") (from Changanassery and Thiruvalla) and [Udumbanchola](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Udumbanchola "Udumbanchola") (from Devikulam and Peerumede) were carved out on 1 October 1956.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kottayam_district#cite_note-1961c-24) After a month, a new Taluk called [Kuttanad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kuttanad "Kuttanad") was carved out from Changanassery and [Ambalappuzha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ambalappuzha "Ambalappuzha").[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kottayam_district#cite_note-1961c-24) The Kuttanad Taluk was transferred into the newly formed [Alappuzha district](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alappuzha_district "Alappuzha district") on 17 August 1957. The Taluks of Thodupuzha and Muvattupuzha were transferred into the newly formed [Ernakulam district](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ernakulam_district "Ernakulam district") on 1 April 1958.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kottayam_district#cite_note-1961c-24)

On 26 January 1972, the three [High Range](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/High_Range,_Kerala "High Range, Kerala") Taluks, namely Devikulam, Udumbanchola, and Peerumede, along with [Thodupuzha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thodupuzha "Thodupuzha") from the [Ernakulam district](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ernakulam_district "Ernakulam district") were separated from Kottayam district to form a new district called [Idukki](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Idukki_district "Idukki district").[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kottayam_district#cite_note-1981c-25) The district of Kottayam took its current shape on 26 January 1972. Now it contains five Taluks- [Changanassery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Changanassery "Changanassery"), Kottayam, [Vaikom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vaikom "Vaikom"), [Meenachil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meenachil "Meenachil"), and [Kanjirappally](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kanjirappally "Kanjirappally").

The municipality of Kottayam was declared as the first town in India to achieve 100% literacy in 1989.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kottayam_district#cite_note-niti-26) The Multidimensional Poverty Index prepared by [NITI Aayog](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NITI_Aayog "NITI Aayog") based on the National Family Health Survey 2015–16 declared Kottayam as the first [Indian district](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_districts_of_India "List of districts of India") to achieve zero multidimensional poverty rate.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kottayam_district#cite_note-niti-26)

## Climate

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kottayam_district&action=edit&section=14 "Edit section: Climate")]

There are no distinct seasons in Kottayam, as it has a tropical climate like that of the rest of Kerala. Humidity is high and rises to about 90% during the rainy season. Kottayam gets rain from two [monsoon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monsoon "Monsoon") seasons, the south-west monsoon and the north-east monsoon, and accumulates an average rainfall of around 3600 mm per year. The south-west monsoon starts in June and ends in September, and the north-east monsoon season is from October to November. Pre-monsoon rains from March to May are accompanied by thunder and lightning; the highest rainfall during this period in Kerala is received in Kottayam. December, January, and February are cooler, while March, April, and May are warmer. The highest temperature recorded in Kottayam was 38.5°C on 6 April 1998, and the lowest was 15°C on 13 December 2000.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kottayam_district#cite_note-27)

The Kottayam district experienced intense [red rainfall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Red_rain_in_Kerala "Red rain in Kerala") in 2001, during which the rain was colored red, yellow, green, and black.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kottayam_district#cite_note-28)

### Legislative representation

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kottayam_district&action=edit&section=20 "Edit section: Legislative representation")]

See also: [Kerala Legislative Assembly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kerala_Legislative_Assembly "Kerala Legislative Assembly") and [Lok Sabha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lok_Sabha "Lok Sabha")

There are three [Lok Sabha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lok_Sabha "Lok Sabha") constituencies in Kottayam district: [Kottayam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kottayam_(Lok_Sabha_constituency) "Kottayam (Lok Sabha constituency)") (6 assembly constituencies), [Pathanamthitta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pathanamthitta_(Lok_Sabha_constituency) "Pathanamthitta (Lok Sabha constituency)") (2 assembly constituencies, i.e., Kanjirappally and Poonjar) and [Mavelikara](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mavelikara_Lok_Sabha_constituency "Mavelikara Lok Sabha constituency") (1 assembly constituency, i.e., Changanassery).

This section is [transcluded](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:Transclusion "Help:Transclusion") from [16th Kerala Assembly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/16th_Kerala_Assembly "16th Kerala Assembly"). ### Taluks

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kottayam_district&action=edit&section=21 "Edit section: Taluks")]

Main article: [List of taluks of Kerala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_taluks_of_Kerala "List of taluks of Kerala")

The district is divided into two revenue divisions which together incorporate five [Taluks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_taluks_of_Kerala "List of taluks of Kerala") within them.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kottayam_district#cite_note-ktmtlk-39)

*   Taluks in the **Kottayam Revenue Division** are:[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kottayam_district#cite_note-ktmtlk-39)

[Changanassery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Changanassery "Changanassery")[Kanjirappally](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kanjirappally "Kanjirappally")Kottayam[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kottayam_district#cite_note-ktmtlk-39)

*   Taluks in the **Pala Revenue Division** are:[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kottayam_district#cite_note-ktmtlk-39)

[Meenachil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meenachil "Meenachil")[Vaikom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vaikom "Vaikom")[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kottayam_district#cite_note-ktmtlk-39)

### Revenue villages

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kottayam_district&action=edit&section=22 "Edit section: Revenue villages")]

Kottayam district is divided into 100 revenue villages for the ease and decentralisation of its revenue administration.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kottayam_district#cite_note-ktmvlg-40) They are further incorporated into 5 [taluks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_taluks_of_Kerala "List of taluks of Kerala") as eludicated below.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kottayam_district#cite_note-ktmvlg-40)
